title: All Three Bits Said Yes

facts.claim: Bloom’s 1970 paper introduced hash coding with allowable errors.
facts.draft_exact_string: Bloom's 1970 paper introduced hash coding with allowable errors.

facts.claim: A Bloom filter inserts a record by setting multiple hash-selected positions in a bit array.
facts.source_selector: turn249761view2 and turn382894view0 NIST PDF mechanics
facts.draft_exact_string: The artifact uses a 32-bit insertion-only filter and three domain-separated SHA-256 probes.

facts.claim: When all positions selected for a query are set, a Bloom filter can report possible membership.
facts.source_selector: turn249761view2 and turn382894view0 NIST PDF mechanics
facts.draft_exact_string: NIST's later analysis describes Bloom filters as probabilistic membership structures: a non-member may coincidentally map only to already-set bits, producing a false positive; for small filters, predicted false-positive rates require particular care.

facts.claim: A nonmember can map only to bits already set by other inserted records and therefore produce a false positive.
